SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0118, resolved 15 Jan 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: bank (cause: bank_details_changed).
Request: ₹64,000 indirect mro, a regular order, vendor V-002, urgency normal.
What happened: the vendor changed its bank account 12 days before the request, on a letterhead scan.
Why the standard process did not fit: the bank check only flags the change; a changed account is a classic payment-fraud route, so it must be confirmed first.
Steps approved (codes): VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, HOLD_PO.
Outcome: callback to the number on file confirmed the account; PO released.
Lesson: a recent bank change means a callback on a known number and a payment hold before anything else.

Failed checks: bank (cause: bank_details_changed) + budget (cause: overrun).

Outcome: parts arrived next day; the callback confirmed the account; payment released after controller sign-off.
Lesson: when a bank change meets a line-down overrun, release the PO but hold the payment until the callback.
